title: Apple's first foldable iPhone sells out on launch in SA, despite steep cost
summary: Apple's first foldable iPhone sells out on launch in SA, despite steep cost
detailed: Apple’s first foldable smartphone sold out on launch day in South Africa, despite the steep cost and reported durability concerns in other markets.
The starting price for the iPhone Duo is just under R50 000, with the 256GB model selling for R48 000 and the 2TB model for a whopping R77 000.
Apple says the Duo redefines the foldable experience, providing the thinnest iPhone with the largest display ever when open - 50% larger than iPhone 18 Pro Max.
While acknowldeging that, at the moment, they're seeing pent-up demand, he cites for instance the continuing demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max which were launched a month ago.
sentences: Apple’s first foldable smartphone sold out on launch day in South Africa, despite the steep cost and reported durability concerns in other markets.
The starting price for the iPhone Duo is just under R50 000, with the 256GB model selling for R48 000 and the 2TB model for a whopping R77 000.
Apple says the Duo redefines the foldable experience, providing the thinnest iPhone with the largest display ever when open - 50% larger than iPhone 18 Pro Max.
The hinge mechanism for the titanium frame is designed for "long-lasting reliability", the tech company says.
The bulk of South Africa's initial allocation of iPhone Duos had already been sold through pre-orders, so those left for walk-in sales were in high demand.
Chris Dodd, CEO of iStore South Africa, tells Stephen Grootes the excitement in the Sandton store where he spent his time on launch, was "unbelievable".
"I think a lot of people just wanted to come in and see what it looks like.

There'd been a lot of hype online, so people were very curious in general and just wanted to get their hands on it."
For those who are serious buyers, Apple provides a range of options to put the pricy product within their reach.

"Our customers can get up to R25,000 when they trade in, so they're using those sort of mechanisms to help fund the devices."
"We also represent all four cellular networks, so customers can choose to fund it over an extended period, 36 months or 24 months, or just buy it cash."
He estimates that 35-40% of the phones sold at iStores are sold on a network contract.
Dodd is confident that strong demand for the iPhone Duo will continue.
While acknowldeging that, at the moment, they're seeing pent-up demand, he cites for instance the continuing demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max which were launched a month ago.
"I think the demand for the Duo will continue as people see others with the phone and put it in their hands themselves.

There's obviously a certain market for it, and I think it will do extremely well."
